# Plan a Week of Family Dinners with a Shopping List Using DeepSeek

> **In short:** DeepSeek is a free AI assistant you can ask in plain English. Tell it what's in season and what you have on hand, and it drafts a five-day dinner plan plus one combined shopping list — usually in under a minute.

There's a small Sunday-afternoon ritual that eats more time than it should: staring at the fridge, opening the same recipe app, and ending up ordering takeout anyway. This guide shows you how to hand that job to DeepSeek (a free AI chat assistant) so you get a real plan, not just "suggestions."

By the end you'll have a five-day dinner plan and one printable shopping list, and you'll know how to redo it next week with different ingredients.

## Before you start
- **Account:** a free DeepSeek account (sign up with email or a Google account at the official DeepSeek site — the button is usually labeled "Start Now" or "Sign In").
- **Device:** any phone, tablet, or computer with a web browser. DeepSeek works in the browser, and there's also a mobile app if you'd rather chat from the kitchen.
- **Time:** about 10–15 minutes the first time, around 5 minutes once you've done it once.
- **Plan:** the free tier is enough for this task. No payment needed.
- **Optional prep:** glance in your fridge and pantry so you can name a few ingredients you already have (rice, onions, chicken, etc.). It makes the plan more accurate.

## Step 1 — Open a new chat with DeepSeek
Go to the DeepSeek website and sign in, then look for a **"New Chat"** button (it usually sits in the top-left corner, next to a small **pencil or plus icon**). Click or tap it. A blank chat window opens with a blinking text cursor at the bottom — this is where you'll type your request. You don't need to change any settings before you start. If you don't see a "New Chat" button, look in the left-hand sidebar and click your current chat title to open a list, where "New Chat" is usually the first option. You'll know it worked when the screen shows an empty conversation with a text box at the bottom and no previous messages above it.

## Step 2 — Tell DeepSeek about your week and your kitchen
Click inside the text box at the bottom of the screen and type a short message that covers three things: how many days you want, who's eating, and what's already in your kitchen. This is called a **prompt** — the instruction you give an AI. Think of it like texting a friend who offered to cook for you, but who can only see what you describe. Be specific about servings and any food rules (no nuts, no pork, picky eaters) so the plan matches your real life. After you press Enter or tap the **arrow / send icon** (usually a paper plane ✈️), DeepSeek starts typing its reply within a few seconds. If your screen looks different — for example, the send button is labeled "Submit" instead — that's fine, use whatever the page shows.
💬 Example: "It's just me and my partner, two adults, dinners only Monday to Friday. We already have olive oil, soy sauce, rice, two onions, garlic, and a lemon. Nothing too spicy. We eat chicken, beef, fish, and lots of vegetables."
You'll know it worked when DeepSeek begins generating a reply (you'll see text appearing word by word) instead of showing an error.

## Step 3 — Ask it to focus on what's in season
Wait for the first reply to finish (it usually stops with a small "stop" square or the text simply stops moving), then send a second message asking it to pick ingredients that are in season this month in your area. This step is the difference between an okay meal plan and a tasty, affordable one — seasonal produce (food grown and harvested right now in your region) is cheaper, fresher, and often already on sale at the grocery store. If DeepSeek doesn't ask first, you can also fold this into Step 2's prompt. After you send the message, the AI rewrites the plan with seasonal swaps. If a reply comes back and the meals still look "off" (heavy on summer tomatoes in winter, for example), just type "Try again, leaning more into [your actual season]" — it will adjust.
💬 Example: "Please redo the plan using ingredients that are in season in my area this month. Keep the meals simple — nothing that needs more than 30 minutes of active cooking."
You'll know it worked when the rewritten plan mentions specific seasonal items (in the northern hemisphere in October, for example, you might see apples, squash, root vegetables, or kale).

## Step 4 — Request the consolidated shopping list
Once the dinner plan looks good, send one more message asking for the shopping list — and ask for it as one combined list, organized by aisle or category. Keeping everything in a single message (rather than spread across the conversation) means you can copy, screenshot, or print it directly. Grocery stores are usually laid out by category (produce, dairy, meat, pantry), so a well-organized list saves you from wandering back and forth. After you send the message, DeepSeek produces a tidy grouped list. If it gives you one long unsorted list instead, just reply "Please regroup by store section (produce, dairy, meat, pantry, frozen)."
💬 Example: "Great, I like this plan. Now please give me one combined shopping list for all five dinners, grouped by store section so I can shop in one pass."
You'll know it worked when the reply is a single tidy list with section headers like "Produce," "Meat & Seafood," "Dairy & Eggs," and "Pantry."

## Step 5 — Save the list somewhere you'll see it
Look for the small **copy icon** (two overlapping squares) that usually appears in the corner of the AI's reply, or simply highlight the text with your finger or mouse and copy it. Paste it into your notes app, email it to yourself, or send it to a partner's phone so it's at the store with you. Without this step, the plan is trapped in the chat and you'll end up improvising at the supermarket anyway. If the list is long, screenshotting the whole reply is faster than copying line by line. After you save it, you can close the chat — the list lives wherever you just put it.
💬 Example: paste the list into a note titled "This Week — Groceries" and set a phone reminder for your usual shopping day.
You'll know it worked when you can open the list on your phone without logging into DeepSeek.

## Step 6 — Tweak it for next week (the easy reset)
When Sunday rolls around again, open the same notes app entry, delete last week's plan, and start a new chat with a fresh prompt that includes what's left in your fridge. This is where DeepSeek quietly pays for itself — week two takes about five minutes and the plan reflects what you *actually* still need to buy, not what a generic template suggests. After you send the new prompt, the AI builds a new plan in the same style. If you find a meal everyone loved last week, mention it by name ("repeat Tuesday's salmon") so it stays in the rotation.
💬 Example: "Same as last week — two adults, dinners Monday to Friday, 30 minutes max. But please repeat Tuesday's sheet-pan salmon, and use up the remaining rice and the half-bag of carrots."
You'll know it worked when the new reply references the salmon and reuses the carrots, and the shopping list is shorter because of those leftovers.

## Common mistakes
- **Mistake:** Being vague in your first prompt — "plan my dinners." **Fix:** Always say how many days, how many people, and what's already in your kitchen. The more specific you are, the less you'll have to throw away.
- **Mistake:** Forgetting to mention dietary rules or picky eaters. **Fix:** Add them in the first message (no nuts, no shellfish, mild spices). It's much easier than redrafting three replies later.
- **Mistake:** Trusting the shopping list blindly. **Fix:** Quick-scan it before you shop. AI can occasionally suggest a weird combination or duplicate an item, and you know your family's tastes better than it does.
- **Mistake:** Letting the plan sit in the chat and never saving it. **Fix:** Use the copy button or a screenshot right after the list appears, while you still remember.
- **Mistake:** Treating the plan as a rigid contract. **Fix:** Swap days around freely. The whole point is flexibility — if Thursday's soup feels more like a Monday thing, move it.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** You skip the 30-minute "what's for dinner?" spiral every week and walk into the grocery store with a list that's already grouped by aisle.
- **For your business or work:** This same "give me a plan + a checklist" pattern works for project outlines, meeting agendas, or weekly content calendars — DeepSeek handles the structure the same way.
- **If you're just getting started:** A prompt that names *people, days, what's already in the kitchen*, and *any food rules* will get you 80% of the way there. The rest is taste.

## Try it now
Open DeepSeek in a new browser tab, type the Step 2 example prompt above (swap in your own family size and pantry items), and send it. Within a minute you'll either love the plan or know exactly what to tweak — both are wins.
